set.body:
Phase G (scale).

Two entirely separate polling paths share no code and no rate budget.

Path A (direct handles): ssh/RemoteTask.scala:148-206. awaitResult seeds a self-recursive poll; each iteration issues one remote.readResult, and SshProcessRunner.process (:121-131) spawns a FRESH ProcessBuilder per exchange. Every 6th poll fires a second exchange for sacct (:180). The code documents the cost itself at :14-15: "Every poll costs one SSH process and one remote agent start". There is NO cross-handle coordination — RemoteTaskHandle (:115-121) holds only its own remote/descriptor/policy, and RemoteBatch.scala:93 runs elements.parTraverse(_.awaitValue), so a 100-element batch runs 100 concurrent private polling loops.

Path B (managed): managed/ObservationCoordinator.scala:68-113 collects up to maximumBatchSize (default 256, :31) and makes ONE scheduler.observe call, with focused probes capped at 16 (:35) and one observer per site (:164-175).

So docs/acceptance/p5-site-scale.md:18's "4,096 active jobs use 16 calls at batch 256" describes Path B only. The same 4,096 jobs held as direct handles are 4,096 ssh processes per tick.

Note also what that 4,096-job test actually proves: bounded scheduler CALL COUNT. Not latency, not allocation, not federation behavior, not site-policy fitness.

Fix: a shared request-level batching service — batched queue observation, selective accounting, batched result reads, connection sharing where safe. Keep durable controller AUTHORITY separate from convenience handles; both then use the same batching service.

Blocked by P8.A2: a shared coordinator built on the broken terminality classifier propagates that hang to every handle instead of one.
set.title: P8.G2: Shared await coordinator for direct handles
